name: Timothy
bio: Timothy, a disciple at Lystra whose mother was a believing Jewess and whose father was a Greek, was well spoken of by the brethren there and in Iconium. Paul wanted him to join the missionary journey and had him circumcised because of the Jews in the region, who knew his father was Greek; from then on Timothy traveled with Paul and Silas, delivering the Jerusalem Council's decrees to the churches (Acts 16:1-5). His further role alongside Paul, and the epistles Paul wrote to him, are told in the books ahead. Timothy remained in Berea with Silas when Paul went on ahead to Athens, with instructions to join him there as soon as possible (Acts 17:14-15). Timothy rejoined Paul in Corinth, arriving from Macedonia with Silas (Acts 18:5). Paul later sent Timothy, along with Erastus, ahead into Macedonia while he himself stayed on in Asia (Acts 19:22). Timothy accompanied Paul from Greece into Asia, then on toward Jerusalem, as part of the group that included Sopater, Aristarchus, Secundus, Gaius of Derbe, Tychicus, and Trophimus (Acts 20:4). Paul later sent Timothy back to Thessalonica to strengthen and encourage the believers there in their faith, and was comforted when Timothy returned with a good report of their faith and love (1 Thessalonians 3:1-6). In his final letter, Paul urged Timothy to come to him, recalling the sincere faith of Timothy's grandmother Lois and mother Eunice, and asked him to bring Mark and retrieve his cloak and books left with Carpus at Troas (2 Timothy 1:5, 4:9-13).
